rules.rule: RENT-BASED CAP: benefit may not exceed Monthly Rent rounded UP to the next $500 multiple (cap = ceil(rent/500)*500; rent already on a multiple stays, e.g. 2000->2000, 1525->2000, 940->1000, 3195->3500). Effective payout ceiling = min(Max Benefit, cap). Formula confirmed in 134/137 cap notes (3 'mismatches' are a different statement, a typo and a total-rent calc).

rent_cap_analysis: Formula: cap = smallest multiple of $500 >= Monthly Rent (ceil(rent/500)*500); 134 of 137 claims whose notes state a cap match it exactly; payout ceiling = min(Max Benefit, cap). Timing: Dmitriy Finkler started noting it on 2023-04-18 (#75 'SD benefit is nearly double the rent amount, should not exceed 2k'). Until ~2024-04 the notes are retrospective ('should not have exceeded', 96 claims) and the claim was still paid above the cap in 61 of them (management paid Max Benefit; e.g. #420 rent 1245 cap 1500 paid 2500). From #539 (2024-04-24) / #575 (2024-05-20) the language becomes 'cannot exceed' (41 claims) and approved == cap in 30, > cap in 8 (goodwill/revisions 1020, 1081, 1150, 730, 751, 799). Scope: enforcement is concentrated on PURE / Treaty T00001: among claims with Max Benefit > cap after 2024-04-24, PURE was paid above cap 16/91 (18%) vs 52/87 (60%) before; T00002 PMs (StarPointe, RentWerx, Blue Fox, Johnson...) 77/127 above cap; Perry Reid (T00003, flat $1,500 max, rents often < $1,000) 50/91 above cap and never capped. Origin: July-2023 'program rules and guidelines' rates table (premium tier by rent, e.g. '$33 per month for preferred tenant is for a $1,500 benefit'); #793 (2024-09) paid goodwill 1500 because 'the incorrect rate has been used for 2000.00 benefit'. Recommendation for the engine: apply the cap for PURE (T00001) claims with claim date >= 2024-05 and any claim with a 'cannot exceed' note; otherwise use Max Benefit as ceiling; flag the rest as 'cap would apply under guidelines'.

Rows 1-10 = the 10 newest claims added on top after the last sort, in descending tracking order (1246, 1245, 1244, 1243, 1242, 1241, 1238, 1237, 1236, 1235; 1239/1240 deleted). Rows 11+ = all other claims sorted by Property Management Company (case-insensitive A-Z), then Claim Date descending, then Tracking Number descending (ties). Utilities: generally excluded; PM-specific exceptions (StarPointe $150 cap per April-2024 agreement; Property Services of Columbus allowed 2025-04; Johnson #683 2024-07 'repairs and utilities').
